notes: On a bare `any` value: runtime key enumeration of the D1 dynamic object's bag in insertion order, `[]` for a boxed primitive, TypeError for null/undefined — matching JS ([TDD-00155](../tdd/TDD-00155.md) Stage 1)
caveats: Integer-like keys are not reordered ahead of string keys — `Object.keys({b:1,a:2,'2':3,'1':4})` is `['b','a','2','1']` (Node: `['1','2','b','a']`); applies equally to `for...in`, `Object.values`/`entries`, spread, and `JSON.stringify`.
A heterogeneous object's values are stringified ([ADR-00492](../adr/ADR-00492.md)); a homogeneous shape returns a real typed `V[]`

A heterogeneous object's values are stringified — its value union is representable only as `any`, whose operators aren't dispatched yet ([ADR-00492](../adr/ADR-00492.md)); a homogeneous shape returns real typed `[string, V]` tuples
notes: Returns a real `[string, string][]` tuple array; destructure with `for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(obj))`

caveats: Every field a source contributes must already exist on `target`'s struct type — a source field `target`'s type doesn't have is a clean compile error (fixed-shape heap structs), not grafted on as in real JS ([ADR-00054](../adr/ADR-00054.md))
notes: Mutates and returns `target`

caveats: Prototype machinery exists on **dynamic (`any`-typed) objects only** — statically-typed structs have no prototype link, and a boxed primitive's `getPrototypeOf` answers `null` (no primitive prototype objects)
`Object.create`'s property-descriptors second argument is rejected until descriptors land
Inherited properties don't appear in `for...in` (own-only enumeration; real JS walks the chain's enumerables)
notes: The D1 prototype chain ([TDD-00155](../tdd/TDD-00155.md) Stage 3, [ADR-00623](../adr/ADR-00623.md)): property reads and the `in` operator walk the chain (own shadows inherited; `delete` re-exposes the proto's value), writes/`Object.keys`/`JSON.stringify` stay own-table — matching JS. `Object.create(proto|null)`, `get/setPrototypeOf`, the `__proto__` accessor (JS setter semantics: non-object values silently ignored), and the `{ __proto__: base }` literal form all work; a prototype cycle throws V8's `Cyclic __proto__ value`

caveats: Dynamic (`any`-typed / js-mode-literal) objects only — statically-typed structs have no descriptor table
`Object.defineProperties` and the descriptor-aware `Object.assign` form are follow-ons; `Cannot delete` TypeError text omits the property name
notes: Real property descriptors ([TDD-00155](../tdd/TDD-00155.md) Stage 5, [ADR-00629](../adr/ADR-00629.md)): spec create-defaults (absent attributes are false), non-configurable redefinition rules, data and accessor descriptor forms. Object-literal `get`/`set` compile to dynamic-ABI functions invoked with the original receiver (inherited getters through the prototype chain included); `Object.keys`/`for...in`/`JSON.stringify` honor enumerability (stringify and spread invoke getters); rejected writes/deletes throw module-strict JS TypeErrors

caveats: Traps implemented: `get`/`set`/`has`/`deleteProperty` — dispatched in the dynamic-object runtime entry points, forwarding to the target when absent ([ADR-00630](../adr/ADR-00630.md)); other traps (`ownKeys`, `getOwnPropertyDescriptor`, `apply`, `construct`, …) are not consulted (those operations forward to the target)
The target must be a dynamic object (an untyped/`any` literal); statically-typed structs can't be proxied
notes: `JSON.stringify` of a proxy serializes its target (spec behavior for data properties)

caveats: `Reflect.apply` / `Reflect.construct` are missing

The metadata API (`defineMetadata`/`getMetadata`/`getOwnMetadata`/`hasMetadata`/`hasOwnMetadata`, TDD-00161 Stage 3) stores on a dynamic-object target and does not walk the prototype chain (so `get` == `getOwn`); `Reflect.metadata` as a decorator factory is rejected
Boolean-returning forms (`set`/`deleteProperty`/`setPrototypeOf`) return the success flag rather than throwing, per spec

Every form requires a dynamic (`any`-typed, or `-compat=js`) target: a statically-typed object operand is a clean compile-time rejection (strict mode does not widen a typed struct to a bag, [ADR-00630](../adr/ADR-00630.md)), including `get`/`has`

notes: Real runtime enforcement, not a no-op: tracks `obj`'s heap pointer in a global frozen-object set, checked at every field-write site, so a blocked write throws a catchable Error even through a different alias/function parameter ([ADR-00055](../adr/ADR-00055.md))

A **dynamic** object freezes via its descriptor attributes instead ([ADR-00629](../adr/ADR-00629.md)): writes/adds/deletes throw, `Object.isFrozen`/`isSealed`/`isExtensible` answer truthfully; `Object.seal` and `Object.preventExtensions` enforce their own tiers the same way

A genuine no-op, not a scope-narrowed approximation: seal's guarantee ("no new/deleted fields") is already structurally impossible for this compiler's fixed-shape objects, so there's nothing further to enforce ([ADR-00055](../adr/ADR-00055.md))

caveats: The key must be a string literal — a runtime-computed key is a clean compile error (no runtime field-name table to check it against) ([ADR-00065](../adr/ADR-00065.md))
notes: Object shapes are fully structural/static, so this is a compile-time `FieldIndex` lookup, not a runtime scan

caveats: Keys must be strings (a `[string, V][]` array) — real JS stringifies any key and accepts symbol keys ([ADR-00348](../adr/ADR-00348.md))
notes: Returns a *dynamic object* (a `Map<string,V>`-backed value, [TDD-00012](../tdd/TDD-00012.md)); read via `obj.field`/`obj[key]`. Seeds via the same `[K,V][]` walker `new Map(entries)` uses ([ADR-00347](../adr/ADR-00347.md))

caveats: `V` is inferred from the first property only
`...spread` combined with a computed key isn't supported yet
The declared-type form (`{ [key: string]: T }`) isn't supported yet
notes: A *dynamic object* — storage-wise a real `Map<string,V>` reusing `new Map<K,V>()`'s runtime, with `.field`/`[expr]` sugar layered on top ([TDD-00012](../tdd/TDD-00012.md) / [ADR-00066](../adr/ADR-00066.md))

Exception: a well-known-symbol key (`[Symbol.asyncIterator]`/`[Symbol.iterator]`, colon or method-shorthand form) desugars to a reserved *static* key, so the literal stays a static struct and the member drives `for...of`/`for await...of` iteration ([ADR-00279](../adr/ADR-00279.md))

caveats: No `this` binding at all — `this` inside a method-shorthand body is a clean compile-time rejection (an object literal has no nominal type to give `this` a shape, and no dynamic call-site binding machinery exists), not silently wrong
No `async`/generator method shorthand either, matching this compiler's class methods ([ADR-00169](../adr/ADR-00169.md))
notes: Desugars to `{ foo: function() {...} }` — a plain anonymous function value, reusing the same closure machinery ([TDD-00060](../tdd/TDD-00060.md))

caveats: A missing key reads as `null` (the compiler's `undefined` stand-in), not a distinct `undefined`; a reference-typed `V` (string/object) returns the `"null"` stand-in on a miss ([TDD-00064](../tdd/TDD-00064.md)/[ADR-00199](../adr/ADR-00199.md))
notes: `.get()` on a scalar-valued map returns `V \| null` — a missing key is distinguishable from a stored `0`/`false` via the presence-flagged nullable-scalar representation

Returns a real `[K, V][]` tuple array ([TDD-00066](../tdd/TDD-00066.md)/[ADR-00201](../adr/ADR-00201.md)); iterate with `for (const [k, v] of m.entries())`; replaced the earlier object-shaped stand-in ([ADR-00053](../adr/ADR-00053.md))

Calls `fn(value, key, map)`, matching real JS's full callback signature — the 3rd `map` argument is the map being iterated ([ADR-00573](../adr/ADR-00573.md)); a callback declaring fewer parameters just receives the leading ones ([ADR-00053](../adr/ADR-00053.md))
Resets size to 0 in place — doesn't free/reallocate the backing arrays ("leak by design" memory model); immediately reusable afterward ([ADR-00053](../adr/ADR-00053.md))

caveats: Accepts only a `[K, V][]` array of 2-tuples, narrowed from the spec's `Iterable<[K, V]>` — the only iterable/pair concept a general expression has here ([ADR-00347](../adr/ADR-00347.md))
notes: K/V are inferred from the entries when no `<K, V>` is given; duplicate keys resolve last-wins; the entries source may be a bare literal or an already-declared `[K, V][]` variable ([TDD-00066](../tdd/TDD-00066.md))

caveats: Accepts only an array expression, narrowed from the spec's `Iterable<T>` — the only iterable concept a general expression has here ([ADR-00159](../adr/ADR-00159.md))

notes: Calls `fn(value, value, set)` — real JS's `Set.prototype.forEach` passes the value twice (Map/Set callback-shape parity) then the set itself; each argument is supplied per the callback's declared arity ([ADR-00053](../adr/ADR-00053.md)/[ADR-00573](../adr/ADR-00573.md))
Same in-place reset as `Map.clear()` ([ADR-00053](../adr/ADR-00053.md))

caveats: Object-identity keys only (a primitive key is a clean compile error); non-iterable (no `size`/iteration — matches spec)

Under `-mm=manual` (default) a weak reference is strong: nothing is ever collected, so `.deref()` never nulls and keys persist ("leak by design"). Real weak semantics require `-mm=gc` ([TDD-00112](../tdd/TDD-00112.md)/[ADR-00349](../adr/ADR-00349.md))
notes: `-mm=gc`: genuinely weak via Boehm disappearing links (the referent word is `GC_malloc_atomic`/unscanned so it isn't traced); a collected referent's `.deref()`/`WeakMap.has` observably drops. `gc()` (Node `--expose-gc` idiom) forces a full collection under gc, a no-op under manual
A `new WeakMap()` initial-entries argument is out of V1 scope

segments.text: - Objects are fixed-shape heap structs — no dynamic property add/delete (`Object.freeze`/`.seal` don't need to enforce this; it's already structurally impossible).
